questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a driving hazard?

options.text: A police car helping a driver on the side of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: An open road
questions.explanation: Accident scenes are hazardous because people may not be watching traffic and the scene can distract drivers. Ice cream trucks are hazardous because they attract children who may not pay attention to vehicles. An open road is not a hazard.

questions.question: How do you check your hydraulic brakes?

options.text: Pump the brakes three times. Then press the brake pedal firmly for five seconds. The pedal should not move.
Pump the brakes three times. Then press the brake pedal firmly for five seconds. The pedal should slowly move toward the floor.
Pump the brakes three times. Then press the brake pedal firmly for five seconds. The pedal should slowly rise.
Pump the brakes three times. Then press the brake pedal firmly for five seconds. The pedal should be easy to push to the floor.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pump the brakes three times. Then press the brake pedal firmly for five seconds. The pedal should not move.
questions.explanation: Pump the brake pedal three times. Then press firmly and hold for five seconds. The pedal should not move. If it moves, there may be a leak.

questions.question: When driving on packed snow, you should reduce your speed by:
questions.correctAnswerText: At least one-half.
questions.explanation: When driving on packed snow, reduce your speed by one-half or more. Slippery surfaces make it hard to stop or turn. You must drive slower to stay safe.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Make eye contact with the other driver.
Assume the other driver doesn't see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume the other driver doesn't see you.
questions.explanation: Always assume that other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians don't see you. Be ready in case they move into your path. You can lightly tap your horn or flash your lights as you pass.

questions.question: Texting while driving a CMV is:

options.text: Okay if the text is work-related.
Okay if the text has fewer than 10 words.
Safer than talking on the phone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not allowed.
questions.explanation: Texting while driving a commercial motor vehicle is illegal and dangerous. This includes typing text into or reading text from any electronic device.

questions.question: A tired driver:

options.text: Should take over-the-counter medicine to stay awake.
Is usually more careful than other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: May make decisions too slowly.
questions.explanation: A tired driver will not see hazards or react as quickly as a rested driver. Fatigue slows your ability to make quick, critical decisions.

questions.question: To help others see your vehicle:

options.text: Turn off your lights during the day.
Use lights only when it rains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your lights clean.
questions.explanation: Keep your lights clean so they shine brightly. This helps other drivers see your vehicle at night.

questions.question: Keeping space between your vehicle and other vehicles is:
questions.correctAnswerText: Important.
questions.explanation: You must keep space between your vehicle and others. This gives you room to stop safely without hitting someone.

questions.question: You should always be able to stop within:

options.text: The distance you can see ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The distance you can see ahead.
questions.explanation: You must be able to stop your vehicle within the distance you can see. Slow down whenever you cannot see far ahead.

questions.question: Your brakes may need repair if:

options.text: The brake pads are not covered in grease.
The brake pads are not covered in oil.
The brake pads are worn thin.

questions.correctAnswerText: The brake pads are worn thin.
questions.explanation: Check your brakes for cracked drums, shoes or pads with oil or grease on them, and shoes that are worn dangerously thin or missing.

questions.question: When driving a manual transmission vehicle, how can you prevent it from rolling backward when starting from a stop?

options.text: Partly engage the clutch before releasing the brake pedal.
Put the vehicle in reverse before moving forward.
Fully engage the clutch before releasing the brake pedal.
Put the vehicle in neutral before moving forward.

questions.correctAnswerText: Partly engage the clutch before releasing the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: Partly engage the clutch before releasing the brake pedal to prevent rolling backward. Use the parking brake if needed to keep the vehicle from rolling back.

questions.question: During a trip, carry-on bags should be:

options.text: Secured so the driver can move freely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Secured so the driver can move freely.
questions.explanation: Bags must not be left in doorways or aisles. They must be secured to let the driver move easily, allow passengers to exit in an emergency, and prevent items from falling on passengers.

questions.question: If a tire fails, you should:

options.text: Wave your arms at other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay off the brakes.
questions.explanation: Using the brakes after a tire fails can cause you to lose control. Stay off the brakes unless you are about to hit something, and let the vehicle slow down on its own.

questions.question: Buses must never carry ____ in the space occupied by passengers.
questions.correctAnswerText: Radioactive materials
questions.explanation: Buses must never carry labeled radioactive materials in areas where passengers are.

questions.question: When planning to drive a bus that has been parked for a few days, you should:

options.text: Assume the interior is in good working order.
Walk through and check that no damage has occurred since the last trip.
Ask the passengers to check the interior.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk through and check that no damage has occurred since the last trip.
questions.explanation: Unattended buses can be damaged. Before driving a parked bus, walk through the interior to make sure everything is in good condition.

questions.question: Tires that are not on the front of a commercial vehicle must have a minimum tread depth of:
questions.correctAnswerText: 2/32 of an inch.
questions.explanation: Front tires need at least 4/32 of an inch of tread depth. Other tires need at least 2/32 of an inch. All tires on the same vehicle should be the same size.

questions.question: When inspecting the engine compartment, you should not:

options.text: Check the coolant level in the radiator.
Check the windshield washer fluid level.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drain the brake fluid.
questions.explanation: When inspecting the engine compartment, check the oil level, coolant level, and windshield washer fluid level. Do not drain the brake fluid.

questions.question: While driving, you should:

options.text: Plan how to avoid dangerous situations that could happen.
Focus only on your own driving and ignore other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Plan how to avoid dangerous situations that could happen.
questions.explanation: Watch the road ahead for hazards. Make a plan to handle any dangerous situations that could arise.

questions.question: When stopping, you should:

options.text: Press the brake pedal down gradually.
Push the brake pedal down quickly.
Press the brake pedal repeatedly, but not hold it down continuously.
Use the same amount of brake pressure every time you stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the brake pedal down gradually.
questions.explanation: Press the brake pedal smoothly and gradually every time you slow or stop. The amount of pressure you need depends on your speed and how quickly you need to stop.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Make eye contact with the driver.
Assume the other driver does not see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume the other driver does not see you.
questions.explanation: When passing a pedestrian or another vehicle, assume they do not see you.
